title: The Date Is Set. Ramayana Drops Its First Trailer July 18 — at India's Grandest Stage.
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's ₹4,000-crore epic will unveil its official trailer at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, with Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and a dream cast expected on stage.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ramayana: Part 1 trailer launches on July 18, 2026, at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
  • The film has a staggering production budget of ₹4,000 crore, making it India's most expensive film.
  • Oscar-winning composers Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman collaborate on the film's score.
  • Dharma Productions secured distribution rights for ₹250 crore, one of India's largest deals.
  • The film's Diwali 2026 release is strategically timed for NRI audiences.

It's the most expensive Indian film ever made, and it just confirmed the most extravagant trailer launch to match.

Ramayana: Part 1 — Nitesh Tiwari's sweeping mythological epic starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama — will premiere its official trailer on July 18, 2026, at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, according to a report by *Variety India*. The event is being positioned as one of the biggest promotional moments in Indian cinema history, and nothing about it sounds modest.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=g6EaI8DsTOw

Director Nitesh Tiwari, producer Namit Malhotra, and a parade of the film's headline cast — including Sai Pallavi, Ravi Dubey, Rakul Preet Singh, and Kunal Kapoor — are all expected to be in attendance. The presence of Yash, who plays Ravana, and Sunny Deol, cast as Hanuman, remains unconfirmed. If they show up, the stage at Bharat Mandapam will hold more combined star power than most award show front rows.

![Nitesh Tiwari — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c2/Nitesh_Tiwari_at_the_%E2%80%98Khidkiyaan%E2%80%99_movie_festival_launch_%28cropped%29.jpg)

A Trailer Three Years in the Making

The announcement caps months of incremental reveals that have kept audiences on a slow, calculated drip of anticipation. An introductory teaser showcasing Ranbir's Rama landed earlier this year and promptly broke the internet — graceful, intense, and dripping with devotional gravitas. The upcoming trailer is expected to be the first real window into the film's storytelling, battle sequences, and the sheer visual ambition that has become the project's calling card.

> **""I have no doubt that the film will break records."

What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRI audiences, the Diwali 2026 release date — November 6 — is perfectly timed."**

And visually, Ramayana is operating at a scale India has simply never attempted. The two-part saga carries a combined production budget of approximately ₹4,000 crore (roughly $500 million), backed by Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios and the eight-time Academy Award-winning VFX house DNEG. The film is designed from the ground up for IMAX, with AI dubbing technology that will enable audiences to watch in any regional language — a first for Indian cinema.

The Sound of Two Oscars Colliding

![Lord Rama — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/45/Lord_Rama_with_arrows.jpg)

If the cast isn't enough, the music might be. The score is a collaboration between Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman — two Oscar-winning composers who have never worked together on a project of this cultural magnitude. Rahman himself has called it "an epic collaboration," describing Zimmer as "almost an ambassador to the world, to non-Indians."

> "His name alone is going to make many people watch the film. At least a section of the global audience will want to see what Hans Zimmer has done in an Indian movie." — A.R. Rahman

Star-Studded Trailer Launch

Rahman also revealed that he was stunned by the film's early 3D visuals, calling the footage unlike anything he had seen "either in India or internationally." When a man who scored *Slumdog Millionaire* and *Roja* says he's impressed, you pay attention.

The Business Behind the Spectacle

![Bharat Mandapam — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/cd/Bharat_Mandapam_Pragati_Maidan.jpg)

The industry is already treating Ramayana like a guaranteed event. Dharma Productions recently secured the Indian theatrical distribution rights for a reported ₹250 crore — one of the largest distribution deals in Indian cinema history. Negotiations reportedly began at ₹500 crore before settling at the final figure, underscoring the enormous commercial confidence surrounding the film.

Trade analyst Vishek Chauhan believes Ramayana could surpass even Dhurandhar: The Revenge, which grossed over ₹3,300 crore worldwide and dominated the first half of 2026. "The buzz is very good, it is a subject very close to people's hearts," Chauhan said. "I have no doubt that the film will break records."

What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRI audiences, the Diwali 2026 release date — November 6 — is perfectly timed. IMAX tickets in Mumbai are already commanding ₹3,000-3,300 for comparable blockbusters, and the international rollout is being planned with the same intensity as a Hollywood tentpole. Reports suggest the team is also in advanced talks for a presence at San Diego Comic-Con later this month, alongside a planned musical event in October featuring a live Zimmer-Rahman performance.

Record-Breaking Anticipation
›Trade analysts predict record-breaking box office.
›Dhurandhar: The Revenge grossed over ₹3,300 crore.
›Strong buzz indicates high audience interest.

Ramayana: Part 2 is slated for Diwali 2027, which means this franchise will own the festive season for two consecutive years.

The trailer drops July 18. Set your alarm.
